perturbations.comparison: Java and Rust are structurally equivalent. Transparent document background, margin expansion, class paint, and arrow channels all survive.
Class body/header ownership is largely correct, but class relationships do not consume arrow LineStyle. Java emits the requested dash pairs on both links; Rust renders both links solid.

Stereotype entity styling succeeds, but class arrows still ignore LineStyle and HeadColor. Java uses stroke-dasharray 6,2 and a #1B5E20 arrowhead; Rust renders a solid shaft and fills the head with the shaft color.

The 9d317115 concrete database/node color and font mapping works, but not every concrete symbol style channel reaches the painter. Java paints the database shadow and node stroke-width 2; Rust omits the filter and keeps the node stroke at 0.5.

Nested componentDiagram concrete selectors are a counterexample. Java applies the document background/margin, database/node paint, database shadow, and arrow color/thickness/dash/font. Rust renders default database/node colors, default canvas, no shadow, and default solid black arrow.
Java and Rust are structurally equivalent. Qualified component stereotype styling and inline color override order are preserved.

Component entity refresh and shaft line styling are mostly correct, but component links do not consume HeadColor. Java preserves the declared #B71C1C head color on both links; Rust fills each head from the shaft color.
Document, state, header, arrow color, arrow font, and dash channels match. Strict comparison fails because Java lays the state graph left-to-right while Rust remains vertical.
The Rust render contains the expected stereotype fill, line color, header/body text colors, shadow filter, and arrow channels. Strict comparison stops at root width/height and viewBox differences.

This disproves the broad state-link snapshot assumption. In Java, the link created before the legacy skinparam still renders with final #1565C0 width 3; Rust preserves the earlier #AD1457 width 2 snapshot. The strict diff also includes the known state direction-layout gap.

Actor and use-case stereotype style values match. Strict comparison fails because Rust uses the actor display label instead of the alias in ids/data-qualified-name, plus a small path-coordinate difference.
Java and Rust are structurally equivalent. Transparent document handling, use-case paint, arrow line style, and arrow label font channels all pass.
Java and Rust are structurally equivalent. Use-case entity refresh and link style capture survive this legacy mutation probe.
Temporal use-case and link style channels match. Strict comparison fails on actor alias identity and a small path-coordinate mismatch, not on theme/style cascade.

findings: The final implementation boundary is af5e6018f5c21a53ea12d02f9470b2bc7fdcd4a0. It is behavior-neutral cleanup after 9d317115, so the substantive final renderer behavior is the 0cfab79b, 1b677826, 025bd4ec, and 9d317115 sequence.

Review1/review2 evidence is preserved at scoped-style level. Review1 is now 7/10 strict and 10/10 scoped-style; review2 is 11/14 strict and 14/14 scoped-style. The remaining strict misses are separable actor identity, state direction layout, or component envelope mechanisms.

Fresh review3 evidence rejects the implementation boundary. Only 4 of 14 fresh heldouts are strict matches, and 6 of the 10 strict misses are direct theme/style cascade semantic failures after excluding known geometry/identity mechanisms.

Class entity and stereotype style ownership has materially improved, but class relationships still do not consume arrow LineStyle or HeadColor. The code resolves arrow_style for lineColor, lineThickness, fontColor, fontName, and fontSize, while dash/head output still comes from relation-local flags or shaft color.

The concrete component symbol fix in 9d317115 reaches simple top-level database/node signatures, but it does not complete concrete symbol style ownership. Database shadowing and node line thickness are not fully consumed, and nested componentDiagram-scoped concrete selectors are a direct counterexample.
Component link style remains incomplete because apply_component_link_style has no HeadColor channel. Java can style shaft and head independently; Rust fills component arrowheads from the shaft color.

The state temporal ownership claim is too broad. The flat state transition probe shows Java applying the final legacy ArrowColor/Thickness to a transition declared before the legacy command, while Rust keeps the earlier source-line snapshot. This needs a Java consumer-specific account rather than a universal Link#getStyleBuilder assumption for all state transition paths.

State document/header/arrow style and autonomous stereotype shadowing now pass scoped style checks in fresh probes; their strict failures are state layout/envelope issues, not style cascade rejections.

Use-case style ownership looks substantially correct under review3. The actor/use-case stereotype, document transparent/dash, legacy refresh/link capture, and temporal entity/link probes either pass strict or fail only on already separate actor alias/path mechanisms.

The audit found no new fixture-shaped production logic in the reviewed range. The rejection is not an overfit finding; it is a model-completeness finding against Java style consumers and selector/value channels.
required_followup: For class relationships, consume the resolved Java arrow LineStyle grammar and HeadColor separately from shaft LineColor, with Java provenance at the consumer.

For component concrete symbols, make componentDiagram-scoped database/node/etc. selectors resolve through the same signature path as top-level concrete selectors, and project shadowing and line thickness into the concrete painters.
For component links, add a HeadColor channel and preserve arbitrary dash pairs and thickness from the per-link style consumer.

For flat state transitions, revisit the Java data flow around stateDiagram arrows and legacy skinparam refresh; update account.json before changing code if the ownership rule differs from the current durable account.

Keep review1_, review2_, and review3_ perturbations as the acceptance matrix. A future boundary should pass all scoped style checks, with only explicitly separate state layout, component envelope, or actor identity strict misses allowed.
